review_reference: Owner decision 33.3 (D-Eminence): "two-person lab check default; a single-person facility may release with a typed, logged reason". Unsigned until the owner signs.
evidence: 0110 (one-person lab check), owner decision 33.3: "two-person lab check default; a single-person facility may release with a typed, logged reason"; unsigned until the owner signs. Written on 0103 (34d6955); 0104-0109 are reserved for other unreleased work and are not on this branch. The declaration lists 0110 and runtime-grants.sql only, on the assumption that production has applied 0102 and 0103 (signed 2026-11-02); if it has not, this declaration must be widened to 0102, 0103, 0110 and runtime-grants.sql, or the release stops with EXACT_SCHEMA_CHANGE_DECLARATION_REQUIRED. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE. Additive only: two new tables (identity.facility_lab_check_settings, append-only, and identity.facility_lab_check_current), two columns on lab.result_verifications (self_check boolean not null default false, added as metadata only; one_person_setting_id uuid null) with a foreign key to the setting row and the check result_verifications_self_check_ck that every existing row (false/null) passes, three new SECURITY DEFINER functions, and a new body of lab.validate_result_governance() (signature, language, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path, owner, ACL and its three triggers unchanged). No existing row is touched; no RLS, FORCE or policy change on any existing table (post-checked). pg_dump --schema-only of a 0103 database before and after differs only by these objects, their comments and grants, the two columns and the governance body. Today's images give the same answers on 0110, except that a same-person check, refused before, is now refused with a coded 23514 message (LAB_RESULT_SECOND_CHECK_REQUIRED; still 500 in today's Lab API). The new Lab API needs 0110 first (its result reads call lab.one_person_lab_enabled()). WHAT IT DOES. A facility administrator (organization.manage at the session facility; admin and org_admin, not org_admin_awaiting_review nor lab) switches One-person lab with identity.set_facility_one_person_lab(enabled, reason): reason trimmed to 10-500 characters, else 22023 FACILITY_SETTING_REASON_INVALID; the same value again is P0001 FACILITY_SETTING_UNCHANGED with nothing written; any other actor, no correlation id or another purpose is 42501 FACILITY_SETTING_PERMISSION_DENIED. Each switch writes one setting row and one audit.events row (actor_type staff, identity.facility.one-person-lab.on/.off, resource facility, the typed reason, details settingId, onePersonLab, previous; ids and booleans only). identity.facility_one_person_lab_state() reads it for the same actor; lab.one_person_lab_enabled() answers the caller's own facility's switch and false without an active membership there. In the governance trigger an invalidated version keeps its old message; a same-person check is refused (LAB_RESULT_SECOND_CHECK_REQUIRED when off; LAB_RESULT_SELF_CHECK_REASON_REQUIRED when on but self_check not asked; 22023 LAB_RESULT_SELF_CHECK_REASON_INVALID when the reason is not 10-500) unless it is an explicit self-check in a One-person lab, which records self_check and the newest setting id (never the client's); a different person asking self_check is LAB_RESULT_SELF_CHECK_NOT_YOURS; release and invalidation are byte for byte 0077's. The trigger holds the facility's current setting row FOR SHARE and the setter updates it: a switch-off waits for an open self-check, and a SERIALIZABLE self-check whose snapshot predates a committed switch-off fails 40001 (the Lab API retries and then sees off). runtime-grants.sql gains a 0110 block: the two tables revoked from PUBLIC and granted to no role; EXECUTE on the two identity functions to hid_identity_runtime and on lab.one_person_lab_enabled() to hid_lab_runtime, all revoked from PUBLIC; the migration makes the same grants. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only, 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): the applier is the owner of schema identity or an inheriting member that may SET ROLE to it (checked first); 0001-0103 applied (0103's identity.organization_application_admin_account md5 186eb4ca420749b8bdb324bdc843bc50); not applied yet; md5 of lab.validate_result_governance() 6bf52a22ce45e834d4f2a194a06babad and of the platform.current_* readers, auth.account_id_for_subject, identity.has_active_membership, auth.membership_has_permission and platform.reject_mutation; the governance function's attributes and its three enabled triggers; organization.manage active and not held by lab; the columns and constraints of lab.result_verifications as 0021 left them; one owner for the function, the tables read or referenced and schemas identity and lab. Negative copies each stopped with nothing applied: governance body changed, 0103 missing, organization.manage inactive, lab holding organization.manage, an owner mismatch, a release trigger disabled, a verification constraint dropped, the table or the column already present. LOCKS (pg_locks before commit on a 0103 copy), held to commit: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on lab.result_verifications; SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities, identity.staff_facility_memberships and auth.accounts (the new foreign keys); ACCESS SHARE on auth.permissions, auth.role_permissions, the replaced pg_proc row, the schemas and the language; no other application table. The file applied in about 0.1 s. Behind an open transaction holding ROW EXCLUSIVE on lab.result_verifications the runner stopped after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied. PROOF on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 (private socket and port, deleted after): upgrade of a 0103 database by the runner (plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back with nothing applied, apply, 0 pending, a re-run 0 pending, the file again by hand answers 0110: already applied); fresh install 0001-0110 (105 files); roles bootstrapped and verified on both, and a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql on the upgraded database changed no runtime role's function or table privilege; all 78 database suites pass on the fresh and the upgraded database, before and after that bootstrap (77 existing and lab-one-person-check, which fails on 0103); a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner and an inheriting member each applied it (new objects owned by the owner), a stranger was refused 42501 with nothing applied; 15 of 15 migration mutants killed by the suite (same-person test dropped, setting not read, self_check trusted for another person, reason length not checked, client setting id kept twice, workforce.manage instead of organization.manage, purpose or correlation check dropped, audit row missing or wrong action, UNCHANGED not raised, the lab read ignoring membership, the state read without permission, the reason not trimmed); two-session concurrency: an open self-check held a switch-off until commit; a SERIALIZABLE self-check whose snapshot predated a committed switch-off failed 40001 and its retry answered LAB_RESULT_SECOND_CHECK_REQUIRED; a READ COMMITTED self-check waiting on a switch-off answered LAB_RESULT_SECOND_CHECK_REQUIRED after it committed; with the row lock removed, and with only an advisory lock, the stale self-check was accepted (both killed). lab-api: tsc clean, jest 484 of 484 (9 of 9 service mutants killed); identity-api: tsc clean, jest 1881 of 1881. The staging schema upgrade rehearsal passed as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (baseline 104, integrated 105, declared 0110, dry run rolled back, checksums preserved, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql, row-level security unchanged on 185 tables, the no-FORCE baseline and the clean install). The release contract needs every prefix up to the newest; this branch adds a temporary, tested allowance for exactly 0104-0109 while 0110 is the newest, and the ledger entries must be re-based if 0104-0109 land first.
